intro: Interest in [biohacking](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/what-is-biohacking) and [longevity](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/women-and-longevity-female-biohacking) continues to grow rapidly: more and more people are looking not just for “vitamins,” but for truly effective tools to support energy, metabolism, and quality of life. What’s important is not the quantity of supplements, but their proven effectiveness and feasibility.
highlights: Longevity boosters range from everyday essentials like omega‑3s and vitamin D to cutting‑edge compounds such as NMN and NR.
Supplements target aging hallmarks — mitochondrial health, inflammation, and cellular repair.
Evidence strength varies: classics like creatine and magnesium are well‑proven, while spermidine and GlyNAC are still emerging.
Smart choices require certified products, natural ingredients, and guidance from trusted specialists.

blocks.text: How we chose these supplements
We evaluated dozens of longevity compounds to build the most relevant supplement list. Here is the four-part standard every supplement had to pass to make the cut.

items: **Human clinical research:** we excluded lab-only hype. Every supplement on this list is supported by human randomized controlled trials or human safety and bio-efficacy studies showing real proven results.

**Safety conditions:** long-term longevity protocols require zero compromise on safety. These 10 blends feature well-established safety records, low side-effect profiles, and high human body tolerability.

**Quality of scientific evidence** : we chose supplements with clear biological mechanisms that directly target the hallmarks of aging — such as mitochondrial decay, oxidative stress, cellular waste buildup, and chronic inflammation.

**Availability** : biohacking should be accessible. All the chosen supplements are legally available over-the-counter, widely produced by reputable brands, and easy to source in pure, standardized forms.

blocks.text: The 10 best biohacking supplements for longevity
Top biohacking supplements for longevity target cellular repair, mitochondrial health, and inflammation. Here are the most popular and relevant supplements for longevity and activity.
Omega-3: inflammation control and vascular protection

Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids are among the most extensively studied nutrients for the prevention of cardiovascular disease and the support of cognitive function. They help regulate inflammatory responses, maintain the elasticity of blood vessel walls, and improve lipid and blood parameters.

In reality, most people’s diets are low in fatty ocean fish, seafood, and plant-based sources of omega-3, so addressing this deficiency is a practical necessity rather than a passing trend. Regular intake of high-quality [omega-3 supplements](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/best-biohacking-supplements) containing sufficient amounts of essential fatty acids from fish helps reduce the risk of atherosclerosis, support heart and brain health, and gently alleviate chronic inflammation.
Vitamin D: immunity, hormones, and muscles

Today, vitamin D is viewed not only as a factor in bone health but also as a full-fledged prohormone that influences immune responses, muscle health, insulin sensitivity, and even mood. Deficiency is widespread, especially in countries with long winters and limited sunlight, as well as among people who spend little time in the sun or use sunscreen.

Maintaining optimal vitamin D levels is associated with a stable immune system, preserved muscle strength, and a reduced risk of reduced bone mineral density and certain metabolic disorders. Since vitamin D is fat-soluble and can accumulate in the body, it is best to determine the correct dosage based on blood test results and under a doctor’s supervision, especially during long-term use.
Magnesium: nervous system balance and recovery quality

A fast-paced lifestyle, constant deadlines, and information overload significantly increase the body’s need for magnesium. This mineral is involved in more than 300 enzymatic reactions, including the regulation of the nervous system, muscle tone, energy synthesis, and the function of receptors responsible for the stress response.

Magnesium deficiency often manifests as increased fatigue, sleep disturbances, irritability, and a tendency toward cramps and muscle tension. Maintaining optimal levels helps stabilize emotional well-being, [improve sleep quality](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/improve-deep-sleep-8-proven-tips), facilitate recovery after workouts, and reduce subjective stress. In biohacking, organic forms of magnesium (such as citrate or glycinate) are often preferred because they are better absorbed and are gentler on the digestive system.
Creatine monohydrate: more than just a sports supplement

Creatine is one of the few sports supplements whose effectiveness has been confirmed by numerous studies. It can help increase strength, improve explosive power, promote faster recovery, and support muscle mass during workouts. For muscles, it helps sustain intense exertion for longer periods; for the brain, it may provide a more efficient energy supply to nerve cells. Studies show that [combining strength training with creatine can help maintain muscle mass and physical function](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6518405/) in older adults as well.
Nicotinamide Riboside NR: from the cell to the body

Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is an innovative form of vitamin B3 that acts as a direct precursor to the coenzyme NAD+. In the field of biohacking, the supplement is valued for its ability to stimulate cellular energy production, support mitochondrial health, and promote DNA repair mechanisms.

The role of NAD⁺ in cellular energy metabolism has been confirmed by dozens of studies. For example, a study published in “Cell Metabolism” showed that [NR rapidly increases NAD⁺ levels](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25424901/) and improves mitochondrial function in muscle tissue. Other scientific publications ([2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28961174/), [2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27656516/)) demonstrate improved cognitive endurance and accelerated recovery after physical exertion. Another important advantage is safety. NR is well tolerated, causes no side effects, and can be taken long-term.
NMN: a longevity gene activator

NMN helps maintain the integrity of DNA molecules and supports the body’s ability to repair damaged DNA strands. This is important for maintaining overall cellular health. NAD+ acts as a coenzyme for several enzymes involved in important cellular processes, including gene expression and metabolism. In the context of biohacking, the supplement is used to slow aging, increase endurance, and improve the body’s recovery, but the study is still on.
Spermidine as an autophagy enhancer

Spermidine enhances autophagy (the natural process of internal “cleanup” within cells) by influencing various genes, including the autophagy gene (ATG5). People who overexpress this gene may live longer. ATG5 expression decreases in response to oxidative stress, free radical damage, and impaired mitochondrial function. Thus, spermidine appears to reverse the effects of these factors on autophagy. Spermidine is also a promising agent for protecting against aging, particularly in the brain, heart, liver, joints, and muscles. These tissues are especially vulnerable to the detrimental effects of aging. By enhancing autophagy, spermidine combats aging in these and other tissues.
Berberine and metabolism in a longevity lifestyle

Berberine is a plant compound valued in biohacking for its powerful metabolic-boosting effects. Due to its similarity to a well-known diabetes medication, it is often called “folk metformin.” It activates the cells’ primary energy sensor, causing the liver to produce less sugar, cells to respond better to insulin, fat to be stored less efficiently, and cells to function more effectively. Berberine smooths out post-meal glucose spikes, protects proteins from “glycation,” and reduces inflammation. It does not directly rejuvenate, but it significantly slows down the aging process and helps the body cope with stress and [modern diets](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-diet).
Curcumin as the ideal anti-aging product

Modern nutraceutical science considers this plant one of the most powerful tools for biohacking. Curcumin properties allow it to work at a deep cellular level. Thanks to its lipophilicity (fat solubility), curcumin molecules readily cross cell membranes and selectively inhibit the enzymes that trigger inflammation.

Even in small doses, curcumin reduces harmful fat levels, protects liver cells from damage, improves memory and concentration, reduces fatigue during mental exertion and stress, and also reduces anxiety, improves mood, and boosts energy.

It acts as the liver’s primary antioxidant defender. It also stimulates bile production and helps eliminate toxins more quickly. With regular use, fat accumulation in the liver decreases, and scarring halts.
GlyNAC: a breakthrough in the fight against aging

GlyNAC is a dietary supplement consisting of two amino acids: glycine and N-acetylcysteine (NAC). Their main function is to provide the body with the “building blocks” needed to synthesize glutathione. This key intracellular antioxidant is essential for our health.

To date, several promising studies have [confirmed the beneficial properties of GlyNAC](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35975308/%20%D0%98%D1%81%D1%82%D0%BE%D1%87%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BA:%20https://bcaa.ua/podderzhka/glynac_kombinatsiya_hlitsynu_ta_n-atsetyltsysteyinu_nac_u_borotbi_zi_starinnyam_u_lyudyny?srsltid=AfmBOoogWoxL03AUXJr7tq-6Dbxvk5dZzzpIfohSE74erPnrQoMCPzYM). When elderly individuals took this dietary supplement, the following changes in bodily function were observed: an increase in glutathione levels to levels comparable to those of younger people; a reduction in oxidative stress; improved mitochondrial function; prevention of endothelial dysfunction; reduced inflammation; improved insulin sensitivity; a reduction in total body fat; increased muscle strength and endurance; and improved cognitive function.

However, despite GlyNAC’s benefits, all of the above indicators began to decline after discontinuing the dietary supplement. Therefore, to support overall health, the supplement should be taken in regular cycles.

blocks.text: Which supplements have the strongest scientific evidence?

Omega-3 fatty acids, creatine monohydrate, and vitamin D have the strongest scientific support. These supplements have been extensively studied and consistently show [benefits for cardiovascular health, muscle function, bone health](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/omega3-supplements-what-you-need-to-know?utm_source=chatgpt.com), and healthy aging when used appropriately, particularly in individuals with deficiencies or increased physiological needs.

A second level includes **magnesium, curcumin, berberine, and GlyNAC.** Here, studies suggest these compounds may support metabolic health, reduce inflammation, improve sleep or muscle function, and help combat oxidative stress. However, the evidence is generally based on smaller clinical trials or specific groups, so further long-term research is needed.

Last, but not least — **nicotinamide riboside (NR), NMN, and spermidine** — represent the most promising area of longevity research. [Early studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35478379/) indicate they may enhance cellular processes such as NAD⁺ metabolism and autophagy, but current human trials remain relatively small and have not yet demonstrated precise improvements in lifespan or long-term health.

It’s also important to note that the FDA does not approve dietary supplements for claims of effectiveness or longevity. However, several of these ingredients have FDA-recognized safety status or are permitted for sale as dietary supplements, whereas others remain under closer regulatory review.
How to Choose High-Quality Supplements

Choosing high-quality, effective supplements is the key to achieving good effects and using them effectively. The wrong choice may not produce the expected results; worse yet, instead of being beneficial, it could actually harm your body. What should you look for when buying supplements?
A specialist will help identify any deficiencies or excesses in your body and select the specific forms and dosages of ingredients that are right for you.
Choose certified products with verified quality, and read reviews not only on the brand’s website but also on independent platforms.

items: **Examine the ingredients and choose natural components**

blocks.text: Avoid supplements with unnecessary additives such as dyes, flavorings, and chemical fillers. Pay attention to whether the active form of the substance is present.

items: **Pay attention to the store’s and brand’s reputation**

blocks.text: Shop at trusted stores that hold the appropriate certifications or from official distributors, and avoid questionable websites and counterfeit products.

items: **Follow the recommended dosages and intake schedule**

blocks.text: Stick to the intake schedule — most supplements are effective only when taken regularly and correctly. Also, pay close attention to the instructions: some supplements are better absorbed with food, while others are better taken on an empty stomach. If a doctor prescribes a supplement for you, strictly follow their instructions.
Are longevity supplements worth it?

Conscious support for the [body’s longevity](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/the-science-of-nad-benefits-risks) always starts with the basics: regular sleep, proper hydration, a varied diet, and physical activity. Supplements in this system serve as an auxiliary tool that enhances the results but does not replace a [healthy lifestyle](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/top-13-biohacking-companies-transforming-the-industry). In today’s world, where chronic stress, irregular eating habits, and sleep deprivation have become part of everyday life, these nutrients help maintain balance in the body. However, it’s important to remember: supplements cannot replace a balanced diet, exercise, and quality sleep. They merely amplify the effects of healthy habits and help the body adapt more easily to stress.
Before taking any supplements, the first and most important thing is to consult your doctor. Don’t make any decisions without a specialist’s advice!
